messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx rate from inference hosts in us-west-2a (usw2a). Alarms: NAT GatewayErr spike, ENI resets, and increased connection timeouts. Autoscaler throttles triggered. Alert links: https://alerts.redwood/internal/1945678901

jasper_oncall: got the page, i'm on it. starting quick triage.

mike_h: seeing ~12% 5xx across inference route us-west-2a, primarily econnreset and read timeout. Fwding small sample logs.

mike_h: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15 10:01:12 WARN connection error to backend g5-12x: read tcp 10.0.1.45:443: read: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15 10:01:13 WARN KV-cache miss spike -> backend retries
```

priya_s: Console -> VPC metrics show increased RxErrors on ENIs in subnet-0a12345 (usw2a). NAT Gateway CloudWatch shows 5xx from 10.0.0.0/16 -> 169.254.169.254 path? Not typical. AWS has no public incident in us-west-2 yet.

irene_ops: can we steer traffic off the AZ? smart-router has cross-az fallback but sticky routing keeps some sessions pinned. Suggest forcing a zone-drain for the inference target group, then update smart-router preference to prefer us-west-2b.

jasper_oncall: agreed. plan: 1) set target-group inference-usw2a to draining, 2) update router preference to -2b, 3) monitor canary traffic, 4) escalate to AWS for host-level investigation. doing step 1 now.

mike_h: running health curl against a few instance IPs in usw2a -> some respond, many time out: `curl --max-time 2 https://10.0.1.45:8080/health` -> timeout.

jasper_oncall: executing drain command on internal admin console:
```
# mark target group draining
POST https://router-admin.internal/api/target-groups/inference-usw2a/drain
# update preference
POST https://router-admin.internal/api/routes/preference -d '{"prefer_zone":"us-west-2b","drain_zone":"us-west-2a"}'
```

deploy-bot: Canary update deployed to 5% traffic -> canary tests running.

mike_h: canary success: latency back to baseline for routed requests. 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 1.2% overall. Good signal.

priya_s: note: some dedicated customer pools pinned to us-west-2a still failing outbound egress to model registry (S3/TLS). We need a different mitigation there (can't just change router). opening AWS support case. Case: 12345678.

irene_ops: For dedicated pools we can either 1) reprovision nodes in us-west-2b and move endpoints, or 2) try to reboot affected hosts. Given ENI error patterns, AWS suspects host NIC or virtualization plane. provisioning new nodes now. ETA ~12-18m for replacements.

mike_h: spinning up replacement dedicated nodes (pool-9876) in us-west-2b, updating DNS TTL low so we can flip endpoints quickly. Commands: 
```
# provision script
./provision-dedicated.sh --pool 9876 --zone us-west-2b --count 3
# lower TTL for endpoints
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://lower-ttl.json
```

jasper_oncall: Customer Impact: broad hosted API impact reduced after switchover; targeted dedicated customers in usw2a still impacted. Support-CM: @support-cs please prepare customer comms for affected Dedicated customers with ETA for reprovision.

support-cs: drafting now. will include: summary, mitigation (provisioning replacements + DNS flip), expected ETA 20-40m, rolling updates to avoid data loss.

irene_ops: AWS replied on case: "We see host-level NIC errors and a small subset of instances experiencing packet drops. We're migrating affected instances to healthy hosts; we've scheduled live migrations. No wider AZ outage declared yet." AWS assigned engineer.

mike_h: after router preference change, global inference latency graphs look stable. Still seeing a handful of backend retries. We'll keep draining until errors <0.5%.

jasper_oncall: creating INC ticket and postmortem stub: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-1945678901. Adding runbook entries for forced-az-drain and dedicated-pool-failover.

mike_h: quick note on rollback: if draining makes any customer see increased latency, we can toggle router preference back and enable per-customer sticky-affinity overrides. Keep that in mind before finalizing.

deploy-bot: healthchecks pass at 95% on canary, promoting to 20% traffic.

priya_s: Dedicated pool replacements booted and passed initial networking tests in us-west-2b. Preparing to reassign endpoints once DNS TTL lowered.

jasper_oncall: escalation: starting a call with AWS ops in 10m (invite sent). Also will handoff to @alex_prodsec in 45m. Current severity: SEV2.

alex_prodsec: ack, i'll take HTO (handoff) in 45. please drop summary + outstanding tasks in the ticket.

mike_h: outstanding: 1) keep draining us-west-2a targets until 5xx <0.5% 2) finish dedicated pool reprovision + DNS flip 3) follow up with AWS engineer on root cause 4) customer comms sent and updated.

jasper_oncall: summary for handoff -> INC-1945678901: NAT/ENI errors in us-west-2a causing econnreset/timeouts for inference hosts. Immediate mitigation: forced zone drain -> router pref to us-west-2b; reprovision dedicated pools in -2b; AWS migration in progress. Next updates in 15m.

incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled at 1945682500 (45m from create). Paging next oncall: alex_prodsec.

support-cs: customer emails queued. Will send 'we're investigating' now and 'mitigation in progress' after DNS flip.

mike_h: monitoring continues; will post final update once dedicated pools fully cut over and AWS confirms host migration.

jasper_oncall: leaving this thread open for the handoff. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
